% Appendix E: Symbolic-pipeline outputs for the surveyed theories.

\section{Symbolic outputs for the surveyed theories}%
\label{SymbolicOutputs}

% Per-theory equation/constraint/term counts used in figure captions.
% Auto-generated by scripts/listings/compute_appendix_counts.py.
\input{sections/appendices/listings/counts.tex}

The surveyed theories are presented under a common reduction: the
linearised equations of motion are evaluated on a uniform magnetic
background $\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$ and dimensionally reduced to
plane waves propagating along $\hat{z}$ (\cref{Linearisation}).
The surveyed-theory campaigns initialise the gravitational wave on
the cross polarisation $\mathcal{H}_{xy}$ (the canonical
Gertsenshtein channel
$h_\times \!\leftrightarrow\! a_\parallel$); the conversion product
is the photon component $\mathcal{A}_x$, at the rate
$\sin^{2}(\kappa \Bzero\,t / 2)$ familiar from the Boccaletti
formula (\cref{Validation}). For brevity the longer listings below
show only this channel's equations of motion plus any torsion
components that appear on their right-hand sides; equations of
motion for the orthogonal polarisation, gauge modes, and uncoupled
constraint sub-blocks are computed by the pipeline but suppressed
in the rendered output. Each figure caption reports the full-system
equation/constraint/term counts so the reader can gauge how much
of the pipeline output is being shown.

Hamiltonian densities are presented as the self-GW + self-EM
sector relevant to the conversion measurement: torsion-coupled
terms are dropped at emission and cross-sector
$\mathcal{H}_{\mu\nu}\!\otimes\!\mathcal{A}_{\mu}$ interaction
terms are excluded from the rendered density, so the displayed
$\mathscr{H} \supset \dots$ is a proper subset of the full
canonical density (cf.\ \cref{DiracBergmann}).

% --- E.4  Propagating PGT with the curvature-squared term -----------
\subsection{Propagating PGT with the curvature-squared term}%
\label{SymbolicMechanism}
The $b_{5}\tilde{\mathcal{R}}^{2}$ curvature-squared term
promotes the metric-perturbation sector to a fourth-order
system. We include this theory \emph{for inspection} of the
resulting equation-of-motion structure rather than as part of
the simulated-theory campaign: the $b_5$-weighted contributions
land only on the diagonal $\mathcal{H}_{ii}$ kinetic equations
(see the $2\,b_5\,\partial_t^{4}\mathcal{H}_{xx}$ representative
displayed in \cref{PropagatingKineticOutput}) and are absent
from the off-diagonal $\mathcal{H}_{xy}$ equation that mediates
the Gertsenshtein channel
$h_\times \!\leftrightarrow\! a_\parallel$. Linear-order
$\mathcal{H}_{xy}\!\leftrightarrow\!\mathcal{A}_{x}$ conversion
is therefore unaffected by the $b_5$ coupling, a null result we
read directly from the equations rather than confirm by
simulation; discussed in \cref{ChannelStructure}.

The Hamiltonian density is suppressed for this figure. The
fourth-order time derivatives lie outside the domain of v6's
no-Ostrogradsky-reduction policy, no published constraint-
promotion Hamiltonian recipe exists for the
$b_5 \tilde{\mathcal{R}}^{2}$ case (Blagojevi\'c and Cvetkovi\'c
2018, App.\,D), and the pipeline's
\verb|ParseHamiltonianExpression| filter does not cover the
4th-order sector. The partial expression the pipeline emits for
this theory is preserved as a comment in the listing file for
reference but is not rendered.

% --- E.5  Ricci--EM nonminimal coupling -----------------------------
\subsection{Ricci--EM nonminimal coupling}%
\label{SymbolicNonminimal}
A single new vertex
$\delta_{1}\tilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$ is added to the
Einstein--Cartan terms (\cref{NonminimalKineticOutput}). The
$\delta_{1}$ coupling generates entries in every
$\mathcal{H}_{\mu\nu}$ equation and second-time-derivative entries
in the torsion sector; discussed in \cref{SectorSurvey}.

% --- E.6  Full YM--PGT nonminimal -----------------------------------
\subsection{Full YM--PGT nonminimal}%
\label{SymbolicGeneralNonminimal}
The full Yang--Mills-form Poincar\'e gauge Lagrangian turns on
$\beta_{1,2,3}$, $\xi$, $\delta_{1}$, $\chi$, $\zeta_{1,2,3}$
simultaneously. The Bahamonde, Barker, and Shapiro variants of
\cref{SectorSurvey} are parameter restrictions of the same
Lagrangian; the surveyed system is collected in
\cref{GeneralNonminimalKineticOutput}; discussed in
\cref{SectorSurvey}.

% --- E.7  Parity-odd extension --------------------------------------
\subsection{Parity-odd extension}%
\label{SymbolicParityOdd}
$d_{14}$--$d_{17}$, $d_{19}$--$d_{21}$, and
$\zeta_{1}$--$\zeta_{6}$ are added to the full Yang--Mills-form
Lagrangian (\cref{ParityOddKineticOutput}); discussed in
\cref{SectorSurvey}.

Under the self-sector restriction of \cref{DiracBergmann}, the
rendered Hamiltonian density for this theory is byte-identical
to the YM--PGT Hamiltonian shown in
\cref{GeneralNonminimalKineticOutput}. This is expected: the
parity-odd invariants contribute only to cross-sector
$\mathcal{H}_{\mu\nu}\!\otimes\!\mathcal{A}_{\mu}$ interaction
terms --- which the self-sector filter removes --- and to an
additional constraint equation, which is suppressed alongside
the rest of the constraint sub-block. The self-energy diagonal
sector itself is unchanged.

% --- E.8  Dark-photon-plasma analogue -------------------------------
\subsection{Dark-photon-plasma analogue}%
\label{SymbolicDarkPhotonPlasma}
A kinetic-mixing vertex $\delta_{m}\,F_{\mu\nu}\tilde{F}^{\mu\nu}$
(with $\tilde{F}$ the torsion-trace field strength) and a photon
mass term $m_{A}^{2}$ are added to the Einstein--Cartan
Lagrangian. $m_{A}^{2}$ enters the diagonal photon
kinetic term; $\delta_{m}$ enters the off-diagonal
photon--torsion entries (\cref{DarkPhotonPlasmaKineticOutput});
discussed in \cref{SectorSurvey}.
